svg.aria-label: How the R360 warehouse process works, from a truck arriving at the gate to an order leaving it, showing the ten hard stops that can refuse it
svg.text: A truck arrives and nothing about it is taken on trust. Ten points compare two numbers that came from two different people — and refuse to go on when they disagree.
Registers the truck at the gate
Vehicle, driver, mobile, ID photo, vendor, PO — under two minutes
Ops approves before the barrier opens
The guard who filed it cannot approve it. Silence escalates at 15 and 30 minutes — it never auto-approves.
Time in is stamped on the entry
Counts the big boxes on the truck
The declared number that everything downstream is checked against
One QR per box. If the count disagrees with the PO, nothing is issued.
Applies and scans every box sticker
A second scan of the same sticker is rejected, not counted twice
One short and the boxes cannot move inside.
One per product box, taken from the PO quantity
Scans each product box into its big box
Over-scan is refused outright; under-scan holds the box
Units scanned must equal the PO quantity
A held box goes to Ops with its scans kept as evidence.
Answers the damage check, closes the box
“None” is a valid answer; leaving it blank is not
Every box now closed, held or rejected
Typed before the warehouse figure is revealed
Their count must equal the warehouse's
Disagree and the entry stays open, with an exception against the vendor.
WHAT THIS APP DOES NOT TRACK
Which rack goods are shelved on. Putaway was removed — receiving
ends at CP4, and where cartons sit afterwards is the floor's business.
What is inside a carton. That belongs to the separate ERP.
Every orange bar is a trigger in the database, not a check in the app.
The same refusal happens from the app, a script or a psql prompt —
which is what makes “zero manual overrides” a property, not a policy.
OCR reads the Order No (CP002458380_0001) and creates the invoice from it
Hands the carton to a packing lady
By scanning her badge off her own About Me screen
The packer must be a second person
You cannot assign a carton to yourself, and the badge has to be live.
Packs it and scans her own badge
That scan is the permanent record of who packed this order
The pack is recorded against the assignee
Someone else's badge closing the carton is refused.
Plans a batch from packed cartons
Planned before scanning, so the two numbers stay independent
Out-scans every carton in the batch
One tap or one scan per carton
Every carton planned must be scanned
One missing and the batch will not complete.
Counts the cartons on the bay
The system's figure appears only after the guard commits to theirs
The guard who counted cannot approve it
No release without an approved count
And no vehicle leaves without a recorded approval.
The cartons are now waiting for collection
Registers the vehicle and loads it
Each carton scanned onto the truck
One missing and the gate stays shut.
Or holds it with a reason, which lands back on the guard's screen
Time out is stamped; the vehicle leaves
The box, or the whole entry, stops where it is
Against the vendor and the PO, naming who found it
In-app and by email, to every Ops Manager
Every outcome needs a note. There is no “dismiss”.
Scanned units enter stock; the gap
The box reopens and its stickers
The goods go back with the
A control point cannot be approved away: where CP2's unscanned stickers or CP4's disagreeing counts are what hold the goods, the app refuses the approval and names what will actually clear it.
